cn_d9f69ddf7a8598b01185.statement: \textnormal{Let F be the entire solution of }F\prime(z)=F(z/2),\quad F(0)=1.\textnormal{For positive real r, find }\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{\ln F(r)}{(\ln r)^2}.
steps: \textnormal{Coefficient comparison gives }F(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{\frac{1}{2}^{n(n-1)/2}}{n!}z^n.\textnormal{The ratio test proves entire convergence and all coefficients are positive.}

\textnormal{Write }L=\ln r,\quad c=\ln 2>0.\textnormal{Ignoring the factorial only for an upper bound, complete the square in }nL-\frac c2n(n-1).\textnormal{The resulting discrete Gaussian sum is bounded by a constant depending only on c, times }\exp\left(\frac{(L+c/2)^2}{2c}\right).

\textnormal{For the lower bound retain the single term with }n=\lfloor L/c\rfloor.\textnormal{Its logarithm is }\frac{L^2}{2c}+O(L\ln L),\textnormal{because }0\le\ln(n!)\le n\ln n.\textnormal{Divide both bounds by the square of L.}

cn_92764936cb2839458f1d.statement: x\prime\prime=u(t),\quad x(0)=x\prime(0)=0,\quad x(1)=1,\quad x\prime(1)=0.\textnormal{Among real measurable essentially bounded accelerations, find the smallest possible essential supremum of the absolute acceleration.}

cn_d1fb1dc5a205ab1e9931.statement: \textnormal{For every positive integer }n,\textnormal{ let }P_n\textnormal{ be the monic polynomial of degree }n\textnormal{ satisfying the displayed equation. Its roots are listed with multiplicity. Find the limit.}\quad tP_n\prime\prime+(\frac{1}{2}n+1-t)P_n\prime+nP_n=0,\quad r_{n,1},\ldots,r_{n,n},\qquad\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\frac1{n+r_{n,j}}=?
steps: \textnormal{The polynomial is a monic generalized Laguerre polynomial. Rodrigues integration by parts shows orthogonality against every polynomial of degree below its degree for the positive weight }t^{\frac{1}{2}n}e^{-t}\quad(t>0).

\textnormal{All roots are positive and simple: otherwise the product of the positive sign-changing factors would have lower degree and its weighted inner product with the polynomial would have one strict sign, contradicting orthogonality.}

\textnormal{Every convergent subsequence must therefore approach the unique nonnegative root of this quadratic. Compactness then gives convergence of the entire sequence.}
